# typed-sql 3.0.0

typed-sql 3 adds lightweight grammar imports, reusable query contracts, explicit live analysis,
and an integrated development workspace. The stable packages share version `3.0.0`.
The TypeScript preview bridge and language server remain experimental companions.

## Breaking change: grammar entrypoints

Application code continues to import `sql` from its selected grammar package:

```ts
import { sql } from "@typed-sql/postgres";
```

Grammar roots now contain the application-facing SQL and runtime surface. Import analyzer
factories and the previous full semantic export surface from the grammar's `/analysis`
entrypoint, and lightweight profile construction from `/profile`. Update configuration
imports and register a lazy analyzer loader when using a lightweight profile.

This separation keeps application imports independent of the full analysis catalog and optional
database drivers. Unsupported, ambiguous, and dynamic SQL still fails closed.

## Highlights

- Query contracts preserve qualified native metadata for exact SQL. Explicit offline, frozen,
  and live modes control reuse and regeneration. Frozen checking does not open native sessions.
- Bounded offline cores and version-owned keyword metadata reduce analysis import costs.
  Optional native qualification covers explicitly supported statement shapes; it does not execute
  candidate SQL or imply universal SQL coverage. PostgreSQL selected routine catalogs support
  reusable offline analysis within their qualified scope.
- CLI and build integrations preserve contract evidence through TypeScript checking, SQL-file
  declarations, transformations, and runtime decoding. Cache inspection, pruning, and semantic
  export diffs make recorded evidence inspectable.
- The development workspace combines SQL and TypeScript editors, split pages, schema and
  relationship browsing, migration history, query execution, and result comparison. Editor
  intelligence uses the optional language server. Trusted live analysis and recorded contracts
  now participate consistently in previews, workspace tools, and captured runs.
- Local ACP agents can inspect workspace context, propose reviewed edits, and present captured
  query data as interactive charts, metrics, tables, and linked filters. Tool permissions and
  project execution remain explicit.
- Migration tools provide SQL and TypeScript migrations, schema evidence, drift checks,
  PostgreSQL history and locking, and inspected recovery.

## Guides

- [Configuration](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/getting-started/configuration)
- [Development workspace](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/guides/dev-workspace)
- [Build integrations](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/integrations/bundlers)
- [Compatibility](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/reference/compatibility)

The runtime requires Node.js 22.11 or newer. Individual adapters and build hosts have their own
requirements. Grammar packages remain independent of database drivers; install a driver only
for the explicit execution or introspection adapter used by the application.
